events.title: Federal Reserve Act Signed into Law
events.description: President Woodrow Wilson signed the Federal Reserve Act, creating the Federal Reserve System as the central banking system of the United States. The act established a network of regional reserve banks overseen by a Federal Reserve Board.
events.significance: It created a central bank to provide a more stable and flexible monetary and financial system, shaping U.S. economic policy and influencing global finance for more than a century.

events.title: Publication of 'A Visit from St. Nicholas'
events.description: The poem 'A Visit from St. Nicholas,' better known as 'The Night Before Christmas,' was published anonymously in the Troy Sentinel newspaper in New York. It was later attributed to Clement Clarke Moore.
events.significance: The poem helped define the modern image of Santa Claus, including the reindeer, sleigh, and chimney, and shaped Christmas traditions in America and beyond.

events.title: Invention of the Transistor Demonstrated
events.description: Physicists John Bardeen and Walter Brattain, working with William Shockley at Bell Laboratories, demonstrated the first working point-contact transistor to colleagues.
events.significance: The transistor replaced vacuum tubes and became the foundation of modern electronics and computing, earning the trio the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics.

events.title: Survivors of the Andes Flight Disaster Rescued
events.description: The last 16 survivors of Uruguayan Air Force Flight 571, which crashed in the Andes in October 1972, were rescued by helicopter after 72 days in extreme conditions. Two of the survivors had trekked for days to find help.
events.significance: The ordeal became one of the most famous survival stories in history, drawing worldwide attention and inspiring books and films.

events.title: Birth of Joseph Smith
events.description: Joseph Smith, founder of the Latter Day Saint movement and the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, was born in Sharon, Vermont.
events.significance: Smith founded a major American religious movement that grew into a global faith with millions of adherents and a significant influence on the history of the American West.
